name: Zestral Yuzu-Ginger Stim Drops
description: Small, jewel-clear hard candy drops containing a regulated dose of synthetic caffeine analog and mild norepinephrine precursor — legal stim-candy, sold in clinical-looking amber vials of 20. Flavor is yuzu and crystallized ginger.
flavor_profile: Sharp yuzu citrus on first contact, then a spreading warmth from real ginger extract, with a clean finish and no chemical aftertaste; the stim onset is felt as a gentle alertness within 8-12 minutes
cultural_context: Zestral Drops are the socially acceptable stim — you can take them in a meeting without judgment. They occupy the same cultural space that energy drinks did in the early 21st century, but more clinical. The amber vial is instantly recognizable.
story_hooks: Arkon Biochem is quietly lobbying to reclassify Zestral Drops as a pharmaceutical, which would require a prescription — the goal is to lock out street competition and increase margins, but it would hurt Tier 2 workers who rely on them.

A runner on a long job discovers their vial of Zestral has been swapped for something that looks identical but provides a much harder stim effect — someone is using the familiar packaging to distribute unlicensed compounds.

A Tier 1 chemist has reverse-engineered Zestral and is selling a homemade version at Φ1.50 a vial; the formula is slightly off in a way that makes it more effective but with a 10% chance of a sharp headache.
